summary: Alberta wooden lookout built 1922 by the Canadian Forest Service, abandoned 1929, NHLR-registered June 1996; the 1996 standing claim is the latest source found.

facts.design: guyed tamarack pole tower with a 7 by 7 ft wooden cab and a log ground house
facts.status_note: Register describes it as still standing at its 1996 inspection; no later source read
facts.agency: Canadian Forest Service (builder, per NHLR); no current managing agency named in sources read

events.note: Constructed by the federal Canadian Forest Service and staffed by Provincial Forest Rangers (NHLR)
Abandoned when a replacement lookout was established at a better location (NHLR)
Inspected May 1996 and found suitable for restoration with the Alberta Chapter of FFLA (NHLR); no completed restoration found

evidence.supports: built 1922 by the federal Canadian Forest Service; staffed by Provincial Forest Rangers
evidence.quote: was constructed by the federal Canadian Forest Service in 1922 and staffed by Provincial Forest Rangers

evidence.supports: guyed tamarack pole tower with wooden cab and log ground house
evidence.quote: The guyed 24 tamarack pole tower with 7’ x 7’ wooden cab

evidence.supports: log ground house alongside the cab
evidence.quote: wooden cab plus a log ground house

evidence.supports: abandoned 1929 when a replacement lookout was established at a better location
evidence.quote: The tower was abandoned in 1929 when a replacement lookout was established at a better location.

evidence.supports: inspected May 1996, found suitable for restoration with the Alberta Chapter of FFLA
evidence.quote: The site was inspected in May, 1996 and found suitable for restoration, which will be accomplished in cooperation with the Alberta Chapter of the Forest Fire Lookout Association (FFLA)

evidence.supports: last wooden lookout of its era still standing in Alberta, probably all of Canada (1996 description)
evidence.quote: last wooden lookout structure of its era still standing in Alberta, and probably all of Canada

notes_for_editor: Single source: the NHLR entry, written around its 1996 registration. Its standing claim dates from 1996; restoration outcome, current condition, managing agency and access were not found in two searches, the firelookout.ca and firelookout.org indexes (no tower-level detail), or the Canada Lookouts Alberta index. facts.status is 'unknown' against the brief's 'standing' until a current source is found. The register's '24' in its pole description is unexplained and left out. No height is given, so height_m is omitted.
